title: Fast Interpreter-Based Instruction Set Simulation for Virtual Prototypes
problem: Interpreter-based instruction set simulators for virtual prototypes have poor performance; optimizations often sacrifice comprehensibility and adaptability.
motivation: Hardware complexity is increasing; simulation-based verification requires high-speed ISS without sacrificing extensibility for architectural exploration.
method: The approach uses caching to speed up software simulation of RISC-V processors. When the processor executes the same instruction sequence multiple times (called a basic block), the simulator caches the results so it doesn't have to re-simulate them—it just looks them up instead. Similarly, it caches memory read and write operations, which are normally slow to simulate. These two optimizations are built into a SystemC-based virtual prototype, achieving high performance while keeping the code understandable and modifiable.
key_novelty: The core idea is combining instruction-sequence caching (basic blocks) with memory-operation caching to achieve high performance without sacrificing code clarity.
contributions: Dynamic Basic Block Cache for instruction processing acceleration
Load/Store Cache for memory operation optimization
8.98× speedup over original VP, 1.65× over Spike simulator
primary_theme: High-performance instruction set simulator for RISC-V
